day.title: Open the app, see today's plan, do it, done.

plan.title: Today's plan is ready
plan.body: Open Sogda and your day is laid out: what to revise, the new words, a grammar topic and a few sentences. About 10 to 20 minutes.

revise.title: Revise what's due
revise.body: The words you're about to forget come back first. Hear it, think of the meaning, then reveal.

learn.title: Learn a few new words
learn.body: Each with its article, its pronunciation, examples, and the meaning in your language. Rate how well you knew it, and Sogda picks the day it comes back.

grammar.title: The grammar topic of the week
grammar.body: A short rule and a quick practice. Get one wrong and the rule is right there.

sentences.title: Sentences from words you know
sentences.body: Practice sentences made only from words you've already learned. Tap any word for its meaning.

done.title: Day complete 🎉
done.body: That's today done. Tomorrow's plan is already waiting.

memory.title: Each word comes back just before you'd forget it.
memory.body: Sogda schedules every word with FSRS, a modern spaced-repetition method. Each time you remember a word, the wait before it comes back grows: a day, then three, then eight, then three weeks. Your minutes go to the words you're about to forget.
memory.chart: A forgetting curve: memory of a new word fades, each revision brings it back to full, and after each one it fades more slowly. The revisions come after 1 day, 3 days, 8 days and 21 days.

voice.body: Your phone’s German voice, or the optional natural Supertonic voice: offline, about 400 MB, downloaded once over Wi-Fi.

languages.body: Pick one language, or two shown together. The pronunciation guide follows your meaning language: Bangla, Russian or Polish letters, or an English respelling. In Russian and Polish, the example sentences and grammar rules too. And the app itself comes in English, Bangla, Polish or Russian.

internet.a: No. Sogda works fully offline. Only the optional natural voice is a download, once, over Wi-Fi.

android.q: Which Android version do I need?

data.a: No. There’s no account, and your progress stays on your phone.

exams.q: Which exams does it prepare me for?
exams.a: The Goethe and telc levels from A1 to C2. Each step has three mock exams that follow their sections: vocabulary, grammar, listening, writing and speaking. They are generated from the step’s words and grammar, not official Goethe or telc papers.

spaced-repetition.title: Spaced repetition with FSRS, explained | Sogda
spaced-repetition.description: How Sogda's {version} scheduler brings each German word back just before you'd forget it: after {g1, number} days, then {g2, number}, {g3, number} and {g4, number} as you keep remembering it. Offline, on your phone.
spaced-repetition.name: Spaced repetition
spaced-repetition.answer: Sogda plans every revision with {version}, a spaced-repetition method that brings each word back on the day your chance of recalling it would drop to {retention, number, percent}. A new word you rate Good comes back after {g1, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then after {g2, number}, {g3, number} and {g4, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} as you keep rating it Good, so your minutes go to the words you're about to forget.

what.heading: What FSRS is
what.body: FSRS, the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler, is an open-source method for deciding when to revise. For each word it tracks how stable your memory of it is and how hard the word is for you, and from those it works out the day your chance of recalling it would drop to your target. Sogda runs {version} with its published default weights, on your phone.
what.target: Your target is {retention, number, percent} unless you change it: Target retention in Settings goes from {min, number, percent} to {max, number, percent}. A higher target brings words back sooner, so there are more revisions a day; a lower one spaces them further apart.

gaps.heading: The first gap depends on your rating
gaps.body: When a new word comes up, you rate how well you knew it with the app's four buttons. At the default target, the rating sets its first gap:
gaps.first: {rating}: back in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

chain.heading: Then the gaps grow
chain.body: Each time the word comes back and you rate it Good, your memory of it is more stable and the next gap is longer: {g1, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, then {g2, number}, {g3, number} and {g4, number}, and after that {g5, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, more than a year.
chain.lapse: Forget a word you'd learned and rate it Again, and FSRS lowers its stability: the word comes back sooner, and its gaps grow again from there.

plan.heading: Revision comes first, every day
plan.body: Each day's plan starts with revision: the words that are due, the earliest first, up to {revise, number} of them. When fewer are due, it fills the rest with the words you're most likely to have forgotten. Then come {new, number} new words, the grammar that's due and a few practice sentences.
plan.wait: Both numbers are defaults you can change in Settings. Due words beyond the day's {revise, number} wait for the next day, the earliest first, so a missed day never turns into a wall of revisions.

why.heading: Why your minutes go to the words you're about to forget
why.body: A word you know well is planned weeks or months ahead, so it takes none of today's time. A word that's fading is planned now, just before you'd forget it. The minutes you have each day go to the words that need them, and each revision you pass pushes the next one further out.

target.q: Can I change how often words come back?
target.a: Yes. Set Target retention in Settings, from {min, number, percent} to {max, number, percent}; the default is {retention, number, percent}. A higher target means shorter gaps and more revisions a day; a lower one, longer gaps and fewer.

missed.q: What happens if I miss a day?
missed.a: The words that were due wait for you. The next day's plan takes the earliest due first, up to {revise, number} revisions, and the rest follow on the days after. When you rate a word, FSRS counts the days that really passed.

offline.q: Does the scheduling need the internet?
offline.a: No. Sogda works fully offline: the scheduler runs on your phone, with no account, and your progress stays there.

grammar.a: Yes. Each grammar topic has its own schedule from the same scheduler, and comes back for practice when it's due.
